semester-8.name: Major / Comprehensive Project
notes: 1. To demonstrate expertise in the chosen project topic, showcasing robust technical knowledge. 2. To apply engineering principles to address real-world challenges faced by industry and society. 3. To develop proficiency in solving intricate problems using a systematic approach. 4. To communicate effectively, both in written and oral formats, with industry stakeholders and the broader community. Details: 6. Students enrolled in the Civil Engineering program are required to select a research topic within the realm of current practices in the field. Collaborative project work is encouraged, with group sizes limited to a maximum of three students. Research areas encompass a wide spectrum including Structural Design and Analysis, Soil and Geotechnical Engineering, Traffic Engineering, Pavement Design and Analysis, Metro and Monorail Construction, Airport Planning and Design, Water Resource Management with GIS and Surveying, Construction Techniques and Management, as well as Environmental Engineering and Energy Conservation. 7. Each group must select a faculty member from the department to serve as their guide. The chosen research topic should align with the interests and expertise of both the group and the guide. Additionally, students undertaking major projects are required to include a one-page section outlining the novelty of their work. 8. Upon completion, the thesis must be formatted according to PDPU standards and submitted to the department through the designated guide. One copy, signed by both the guide and the Head of the Department, will be archived in the departmental library for record-keeping and to verify originality. A review committee consisting of at least two faculty members will assess the internal components of the project and dissertation work, while the external review panel will include an external examiner, the department head, and the guide.

semester-8.name: Major Project OR Comprehensive Project
notes: 1. To design and execute independent biotechnology research projects 2. To demonstrate effective scientific communication skills in both written and oral formats 3. To critically evaluate the potential of biotechnology to address global challenges in healthcare, agriculture, and industry. 4. To master laboratory techniques essential for biotechnology research 5. Medical Biotechnology: o Drug development and discovery: Identify new drug targets, develop novel therapeutics (small molecules, antibodies, gene therapies) for diseases, and optimize drug delivery systems. o Diagnostics: Use tools like PCR, biosensors, and next-generation sequencing to design rapid and sensitive diagnostics for infectious diseases, cancers, and genetic disorders. o Regenerative medicine: Focus on tissue engineering, stem cell therapies, and biomaterial development for repairing or replacing damaged organs and tissues. o Personalized medicine: Use genomics, proteomics, and bioinformatics to tailor diagnosis and treatment strategies to an individual's genetic makeup. o Biopharmaceutical Development: Scale-up production of biologics such as vaccines, monoclonal antibodies, and biosimilars using recombinant DNA technology. Explore fermentation and cell culture techniques for high-yield production. o Nanomedicine: Develop nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems for targeted therapies. Design nanoparticles for imaging, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases like cancer and cardiovascular disorders. 6. Bioinformatics: o Molecular Modelling and Drug Design: Focuses on using machine learning and deep learning algorithms to predict the three-dimensional structure of proteins, vital for understanding protein function and advancing drug design. o Disease Association Studies: Targets the identification of genetic variants linked to diseases by analyzing large-scale genomic data, aiming to uncover the genetic basis of complex diseases and improve diagnostics and therapies. o Multi-Omics Integration: Involves integrating genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and other 'omics' data to gain a comprehensive understanding of biological systems, aiding in the discovery of new biomarkers and therapeutic targets. o Computational Systems Biology: Modeling and simulating biological systems using mathematical modeling, network analysis, and high-throughput data to decipher the mechanisms of biological processes and pathways. 7. Agricultural Biotechnology: o Crop improvement: Enhance crop yields, stress tolerance (drought, salinity), and nutritional value of crops through genetic engineering or CRISPR-based gene editing. o Pest and disease management: Develop bio pesticides and disease-resistant crops to reduce reliance on chemical inputs. o Sustainable agriculture: Use microbes for nutrient optimization, study plant-microbe interactions, and develop strategies to improve soil health. 8. Industrial Biotechnology: o Biofuel production: Develop microbial systems for converting biomass into bioethanol, biodiesel, and other biofuels. o Bioremediation: Harness the power of microbes or enzymes to clean up contaminated environments (oil spills, polluted water). o Bio-based materials production: Create sustainable alternatives to plastics, textiles, and other materials using bio-resources. 9. Environmental Biotechnology: o Wastewater treatment: Design innovative microbial systems for effective treatment of industrial and municipal wastewater. o Biomonitoring: Biosensors and microorganisms are used to assess environmental quality and detect pollutants. o Biodiversity conservation: Apply biotechnology tools for analyzing species diversity and developing conservation strategies. 10. Additional Research Areas 11. Food Biotechnology: Improving food safety, preservation, nutritional value, flavor profiles, waste reduction 12. Marine Biotechnology: Exploring marine organisms and their bioactive compounds for pharmaceutical and industrial applications and understanding ocean ecosystems. 13. Forensic Biotechnology: Using DNA analysis and other biotechnological tools in criminal investigations.

units.title: Unit 1
topics: The moral question is a subjective and relative question

topics: Is what ismorally good commanded by God because it is morally good, or is it morally good because it is commanded by God?” Ever since Plato’s original discussion

topics: Utilitarianism is defined as the science of utility

racism was justified as a utilitarian principle
Individualism questions the greatest benefit to greatest number theory
This unit will open up the thinking of students to various ways in which they can imagine their role in society as professionals
A question they should ask of themselves is “Do | want to be the best
best engineer/student/individual or do | want to be the best good engineer/student/individual?”

topics: This unit lays bare the Rawlsian difference between the “Good thing” and the “Right thing

a debate on public good” can be initiated
